task_title: Fix ws-mesh rotated-run selftest collision classification
task_criteria: The ws-mesh rotated-run acceptance passes in a CI-like environment when an unrelated listener occupies the first candidate: the runner must rotate to a free selected port, start its own relay there, preserve the foreign listener, and prove the selected port is served; the selftest must not report a product failure for a runner-side bind collision.

items.criterion: The ws-mesh rotated-run acceptance passes in a CI-like environment when an unrelated listener occupies the first candidate: the runner must rotate to a free selected port, start its own relay there, preserve the foreign listener, and prove the selected port is served; the selftest must not report a product failure for a runner-side bind collision.
items.detail: Rotation + own relay + foreign-listener preservation + selected-port proof all verified live: `python3 examples/scratch-port-rotation-selftest.py --case ws-mesh-rotate` -> exit 0, 'PASS: ws-mesh-rotate (11 checks)' with 'ok ws-mesh: the occupied FIRST candidate :37880 was rotated past to :37881', 'ok ws-mesh: the rotated run still succeeds — no false skip (exit 0 after 3.5s)', 'ok ws-mesh: the holder of :37880 was left running (a foreign listener is not ours to kill)', 'ok ws-mesh: the relay answering /health is the pid this run started (:37881)'. Collision classification: is_startup_bind_collision (examples/scratch-port-rotation-selftest.py:881-901) requires the ws-mesh runner, rc!=0, a selected port, '[2/10] start relay on :<port>' before the diagnostic, the diagnostic naming that port, no '[3/10] HTTP-register' before it, no ':<port> is held by pid' ownership-guard line, and no PASS marker; the diagnostic string matches the real product (cmd/server/main.go:1573 'server failed: another process already holds this port (bind: address already in use)'). case_rotate:916-949 then discards the block, re-picks a fresh one and retries within ROTATION_SETUP_RETRIES=3, reporting SETUP exhaustion (:942-944) rather than a product failure. `--case ws-mesh-setup-collision` -> exit 0, 'PASS: ws-mesh-setup-collision (5 checks)' including 'ok ws-mesh: the selected-port setup collision triggers one bounded fresh-block retry (runner attempts=2)'. Full suite `python3 examples/scratch-port-rotation-selftest.py` -> EXIT=0, 'scratch-port-rotation-selftest: 12/12 case(s) behaved', no FAIL lines. CI reachability: .github/workflows/ci.yml:160 `make scratch-port-rotation-selftest` -> Makefile:378-379. Go suite `go test -short -count=1 ./...` had one load-sensitive failure in internal/relay TestSubscribePongingSubscriberSurvives (keepalive_test.go:423, '1m loadavg 29.90'); re-run alone `go test -short -count=1 -run TestSubscribePongingSubscriberSurvives ./internal/relay/` -> 'ok github.com/crier-dev/crier/internal/relay 1.085s', EXIT=0 — unrelated to this diff, which touches only examples/scratch-port-rotation-selftest.py and .gitreins/tasks.yaml.

items.criterion: The retry path is reachable from the real runner, not only from the fake: the classifier's required diagnostic is the one the shipped crier server actually emits on EADDRINUSE, and the runner's own output shape ([2/10] start relay on :<port>) matches what run-demo.sh prints.
items.detail: cmd/server/main.go:1573 emits exactly 'server failed: another process already holds this port (bind: address already in use)' on EADDRINUSE (logServeFailure, guarded by errors.Is(err, syscall.EADDRINUSE)); examples/ws-mesh-demo/run-demo.sh:284 prints '==> [2/10] start relay on :${DEMO_PORT} (auth-disabled)'. Direct probe of the classifier with a realistic transcript (server ERROR line + 'FAIL: relay exited during startup (pid 1234)', no ownership line, no [3/10]) returned True.

items.criterion: A genuine product failure on the same selected port is NOT reclassified as setup loss (no masking of real regressions).
items.detail: Probe of is_startup_bind_collision: ownership-guard product failure (':25001 is held by pid 999 == our relay pid 1234' + 'NOT the process holding :25001 — refusing to measure it') -> False; transcript containing the PASS marker -> False; the federation runner with the same text -> False. The in-suite control also asserts this: 'ok ws-mesh: a behavior-stage failure is not classified as setup recovery' and 'ok ws-mesh: a zero exit cannot be classified as a bind collision' (examples/scratch-port-rotation-selftest.py:1165-1168).

items.criterion: The retry is bounded and terminates: exhaustion reports a SETUP failure rather than looping or silently passing.
items.detail: ROTATION_SETUP_RETRIES = 3 (examples/scratch-port-rotation-selftest.py:879); the loop is `for attempt in range(ROTATION_SETUP_RETRIES)` (:916) and on the last attempt records 'SETUP selected-port bind collision recovery exhausted' and returns (:942-944). Observed in the live run: 'ws-mesh: SETUP selected port :27668 was lost at bind; fixture listener :27667 remains listening; retrying on a fresh block (attempt 1/3)' followed by a PASS, i.e. exactly one retry then termination.

items.criterion: The foreign listener that occupied the first candidate is preserved (never killed) across rotation and retry.
items.detail: squatter.still_listening() is part of fixture_ok (:939) and is asserted again at :968-969; squatter.close() appears only in the finally block (:971-972), so the fixture socket is released by the selftest itself, never signalled. Live evidence: 'ok ws-mesh: the holder of :37880 was left running (a foreign listener is not ours to kill)' and 'ok ws-mesh: no squatter was disturbed by either run'.

items.criterion: The new case is reachable from the CI entrypoint (make target invoked by the workflow) and the whole selftest still exits 0.
items.detail: .github/workflows/ci.yml:160 runs `make scratch-port-rotation-selftest`; Makefile:378-379 runs `python3 examples/scratch-port-rotation-selftest.py`; the new case is registered in CASES (:138), CASE_TOOLS (:169) and the main() dispatch (:1287-1288). Full run: EXIT=0, 'scratch-port-rotation-selftest: 12/12 case(s) behaved', 12 'PASS:' lines, zero 'FAIL' lines.
